description: Single source of truth for storage retention (AL-01/AL-04). Declares, per repo-relative directory, the artifact class, TTL, and expiry action enforced by libs/core/storage-janitor.ts. AL-04 extends the AL-01 seed to full coverage of active/shared/runtime/, active/shared/exports/ and active/archive/: every directory is either TTL-governed or declared action=review_required (no automatic deletion; surfaced in the janitor report for a human decision — never a silent forever-retention). Entries with audit=true leave a deletion audit record in active/shared/logs/audit/storage-retention.jsonl; entries with soft_delete_days move expired files to active/archive/.trash/<original-path> for that many further days before the trash sweep purges them. Directories not declared here are never deleted by the janitor; runtime/ subdirectories without an entry are surfaced in the janitor report as uncovered. EV-06 extends coverage beyond active/shared/runtime/ to the append-only event stores (active/shared/observability/, active/shared/coordination/orchestration/events/, presence/bridge/runtime/): these sat outside every janitor scan root, so they were neither TTL-governed nor surfaced as uncovered. scanEventStores enforces their TTLs and listUncoveredEventStoreDirs reports undeclared event streams. WI-10 declares the work-inventory personal/member knowledge subtrees (knowledge/personal/work-inventory, knowledge/personal/members) as never-auto-delete evidence. WI-16 adds an entry-level status_rules vocabulary — a generic, declarative per-file status+age expiry rule nested under a directory entry — and uses it on knowledge/personal/members to expire stale pending_review and discarded work-inventory observation summaries by their own JSON status/date fields (see storage-janitor.ts's sweepStatusRules) without touching confirmed summaries, consents, or unrelated member records. G01/G02/G14 (ops-runtime-retention) declare the top-level ledgers and state files that sit directly in active/shared/runtime/ (dot-*.jsonl, mission_queue.jsonl, reasoning-failover-events.jsonl, …) and the remaining runtime subdirectories; listUncoveredRuntimeEntries now reports undeclared top-level files too (janitor report field uncoveredRuntimeFiles), and the runtime-store-retention check gate (scripts/check_runtime_store_retention.ts) fails when source references an active/shared/runtime/<name> store with no entry here. Top-level file entries carry no ttl_days: the janitor's mtime TTL walks directories and an append-only ledger's mtime never ages, so such files are either self-bounded (the note says how) or review_required.

entries.note: Formerly DEFAULT_TMP_TTL_MS (24h). Shared scratch floor — anything here is consumable by contract. Partitioned as tmp/system/<domain>/ or tmp/<tier>/<tenant|shared>/<domain>/ (libs/core/storage-layout.ts); unpartitioned subtrees are legacy call sites ratcheted by shared-tmp-allowlist.json.

Storage-layout staging floor: inbound external files copied in for perception / ingest (staging/<partition>/<domain>/<job>/). Consumed by ingest; a short grace beyond the tmp TTL covers multi-day review of an inbound batch.

Storage-layout cache floor root. Unpartitioned legacy files here (knowledge-index ki-*.json) are self-managed: knowledge-index evicts them by its own ki-usage.json LRU, which mtime cannot see, so the root carries no directory TTL. Partitions below carry the TTL.

Storage-layout cache partition (system): derived, re-generable data (digest-keyed sidecars, model/build trees). Deletion only costs a rebuild; anything that cannot be rebuilt belongs in runtime/ state instead.

Storage-layout cache partition (public): derived, re-generable data (digest-keyed sidecars, model/build trees). Deletion only costs a rebuild; anything that cannot be rebuilt belongs in runtime/ state instead.

Storage-layout cache partition (confidential): derived, re-generable data (digest-keyed sidecars, model/build trees). Deletion only costs a rebuild; anything that cannot be rebuilt belongs in runtime/ state instead.

Storage-layout cache partition (personal): derived, re-generable data (digest-keyed sidecars, model/build trees). Deletion only costs a rebuild; anything that cannot be rebuilt belongs in runtime/ state instead.

Transpile cache of scripts/ts-loader.mjs (scripts/ts-loader-cache.mjs): one file per (loader version, TypeScript version, options, path, source hash), written by temp-file + rename. Every edit of a source adds an entry and orphans the old one, so a 7-day mtime TTL bounds growth; a deleted entry only costs one re-transpile. Repository code only (data trees active/, knowledge/, customer/, vault/ are never cached). Kill switch KYBERION_TS_LOADER_CACHE=0.

Cross-process local STT discovery result (libs/core/local-stt-discovery.ts): one candidates.json rewritten atomically, keyed by platform, PATH and registry content, valid for KYBERION_STT_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS (default 10 min). Host binary paths and versions only; deleting it costs one probe.

Storage-layout artifact floor: system- and tenant-owned deliverables written by writeScopedArtifact (artifacts/system/<class>/, artifacts/<tier>/<tenant|shared>/<class>/). Deliverables are never silently expired; mission/project-owned artifacts live in their scope directories instead.

Durable tenant/tier-partitioned local-pad records, payloads, artifacts, handoffs, and rebuildable indexes. Retention is policy-specific; janitor must surface for an operator decision rather than deleting capture history.
Formerly DEFAULT_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS. Covers audit/process/surfaces/traces log subtrees.
Browser execution evidence — kept ~90d to align with audit retention (review finding OP-M3).
Self-repair artifacts — short-lived until promoted.
Approval requests and events written by test runs (approval-store.ts approvalStoreRoots under vitest). Isolated from the live approval store so fixtures never count as operator decisions.

Delivery outboxes, audit logs, ops alerts, inboxes and peer mailboxes written by test runs (path-resolver vitestLivePath under vitest). Kept out of the live operational tree so fixtures are never delivered or counted as evidence.
Per-process operations-halt flags written by test runs (operations-halt.ts under vitest). Isolated so a test that engages a halt never stops the live system.
Conversation signal ledger (libs/core/intent/conversation-signals.ts): one JSONL file per month of turn outcomes — metadata and a short excerpt, never a tenant turn. Read by the conversation report.
A2A conversation transcripts.
Self-expiring: each JSON entry carries its own expiresAt, honored per-file by the janitor. No directory-level TTL.
Generated system/janitor reports. Deletions are audited and get a 14d trash grace because reports are sometimes referenced as evidence after the fact.
Runtime health history (runtime-health-history.ts) — log-like time series, aligned with report retention.
TTS loopback verification receipts (tts-loopback-verifier.ts) — execution evidence, same 90d as browser-receipts, audited with a 30d trash grace.
Peer conversation transcripts (peer-conversation.ts) — same retention as a2a-conversations.
History search index (history-search-index.ts) — regenerable from source logs.
Baseline-check / provider-capability probe cache — regenerated on the next session start.
Apple Intelligence bridge spool (apple-intelligence-bridge.ts) — request/response intermediates.
Distill candidate staging (distill-candidate-registry.ts) — candidates either promote into knowledge/ or expire; previously unbounded (~97 files).
Promotion-candidate staging (promotion-candidates.ts) — same promote-or-expire contract as distill-candidates.
Daemon heartbeat files (daemon-heartbeat.ts). Live daemons refresh mtime continuously, so a 14d TTL only ever removes entries of long-dead daemons.
A2A envelope-signature / peer identity state (a2a-envelope-signature.ts) — load-bearing trust material, no automatic deletion.
Agent runtime supervisor state — load-bearing while supervised runtimes exist.
Artifact-record store payloads (artifact-record.ts) referenced by artifact_id — deleting by TTL would break references; lifecycle belongs to AL-02/AL-03 scoped closure.
Audit chain integrity state (chain-integrity.ts) — never auto-delete audit material.
Background-review patches/records referenced by approval requests — load-bearing while a review is pending.
Browser conversation-session state (browser-conversation-session.ts).
Computer-surface session state (computer-surface.ts).

Resident-dot state (dot-state-paths.ts DOT_STATE_ROOT): events.jsonl inbound-event ledger, work-results / kr-ledger / outcomes / autonomy / arbitration ledgers and working memory, per scope (system floor or tenants/<slug>/). Load-bearing append-only state — event dedup and trigger replay read the ledger tail (bounded at 4 MiB), outcome checks and autonomy read the result ledgers. No automatic deletion; a tenant subtree is purged by the audited tenant offboarding ceremony.

DA-08: ingest dedup content-hash registry (content-hash-registry.jsonl, ingest-actuator dedup.ts) — load-bearing append-only dedup state; TTL deletion would re-open duplicate ingests. Tenant lines are pruned only by the audited tenant offboarding ceremony (scope-offboarding.ts).
DA-08: per-tenant daily ingest quota counters (ingest-quota.ts) — one JSON per tenant per UTC day; only the current day is load-bearing, older counters expire after 30d.
DA-03/DA-08: incremental sync cursor state per tenant/source — live state, never TTL-deleted; a tenant's subtree is purged by the audited tenant offboarding ceremony (scope-offboarding.ts).
Cross-process lock files (src/lock-utils.ts) — deleting a held lock breaks mutual exclusion.
Generation scheduler job queue (generation-scheduler.ts) — load-bearing while jobs are pending.
Per-tenant daily abstract generation-unit counters (generation-quota.ts); historical cost remains in the usage ledger, while only the current quota window is load-bearing.

Memory promotion queue (memory-promotion-queue.ts) — pending promotions are un-regenerable learning. Tenant-scoped candidates live under active/shared/runtime/tenants/<tenant>/memory; the global path is retained for legacy/unscoped records until reviewed.
OAuth token/flow state — credentials, never TTL-deleted.
Peer messaging queues (peer-messaging.ts) — undelivered messages are load-bearing.
Surface presence coordination state (surface-coordination-store.ts).
Presence-studio workflow state (email-workflow.ts).
Project track state (mission-context-pack.ts) — load-bearing across missions.
Project registry (project-registry.ts) — load-bearing registry.
Service binding registry (service-binding-registry.ts) — connection state, never TTL-deleted.
Session-scoped volatile workspaces (path-resolver volatile('session')). GC'd by scope-linked mission-archive GC (AL-04, mission-maintenance.ts), not by TTL.
Miscellaneous runtime state incl. janitor-last-run marker and reasoning failover state (reasoning-failover.ts).
Surface runtime state (surface-runtime.ts) — load-bearing for running surfaces.
Task-session records (task-session.ts). GC'd per mission by scope-linked mission-archive GC (AL-04), not by TTL.
Terminal bridge session state (terminal-bridge.ts).

Tenant-sharded knowledge delivery, usage aggregate, human feedback, gap, and promotion telemetry. Tenant subtrees are removed only through audited offboarding; the unscoped legacy lane remains review-only.
Physical tenant runtime namespaces for scoped intent, cowork, and other load-bearing state. Never TTL-delete; remove only through audited tenant offboarding.
System-level intent contract seed/runtime snapshot. Tenant-scoped entries must migrate to active/shared/runtime/tenants/<tenant>; the global snapshot is never TTL-deleted.
Cowork synchronization checkpoint. Preserve as load-bearing state until a tenant-specific replacement is verified.
Tenant-sharded observability streams. Keep a quarterly audit window; tenant offboarding exports and removes the matching namespace first.
Tenant-sharded coordination state not covered by a surface-specific root. Removal is owned by audited offboarding.
Tenant-bound personal knowledge overlay. Never TTL-delete; offboarding must export and remove only the matching tenant subtree.
Voice profile registry (voice-profile-registry.ts) — user-facing configuration, never TTL-deleted.
Work-item claim/coordination state (work-coordination.ts) — deleting live claims breaks the write-exclusion contract.
Same-checkout co-session presence/leases/handoffs (co-session.ts) — deleting live leases breaks multi-provider write exclusion.

WS-05 per-session workspaces and their ledger (workspace-ledger.ts). The generic TTL janitor never deletes here; the janitor workspace sweep (sweepWorkspaces) removes only ledger-registered orphans past the workspace-budget-policy.json orphan TTL, and unregistered directories are reported, never deleted.
WS-01 private per-session git index files registered in the workspace ledger (kind git-index). Same contract as active/shared/runtime/workspaces: deleted only through the ledger sweep, never by TTL.
Mesh hub delivery and peer state; tenant-scoped records are removed only through audited offboarding.
Pipeline run records are evidence-linked and must be retained until the owning mission closes.
Execution graph records are load-bearing lineage and require scope-linked cleanup.

G01: append-only resident-dot wake ledger (libs/core/dot/dot-runtime.ts). Load-bearing history: a delivered/rejected trigger key stays consumed forever, so truncating it would re-fire old inbox/watch/event wakes — never TTL-deleted. Hot-path reads (due-ness, wake circuit, per-skip dedupe) replay it incrementally via readJsonLinesCached (libs/core/jsonl-tail.ts), parsing only rows appended since the previous call.

G01: append-only per-wake dot token usage (dot-runtime.ts recordDotTokenUsage), read by dotTokensUsedToday and org-budget-governor for the current UTC day only. Usage-accounting history, so no automatic deletion; dotTokensUsedToday replays it incrementally (readJsonLinesCached) instead of parsing the whole history per call. Archive old days by operator decision.

G01: dot wake inbox (libs/core/dot/dot-inbox.ts). Wake trigger keys hash the row's line index, so truncating or rewriting the file would re-key and re-fire every row — never TTL-deleted or compacted in place.
G01: dot charter lifecycle audit trail (dot-charter.ts / dot-lifecycle.ts). Audit evidence — human retention decision only.
G01: append-only dot action snapshots (dot-action-ledger.ts / dot-dispatch.ts); dispatch and recovery replay it, so it is load-bearing state.
Dot digest delivery ledger (dot-dispatch.ts DOT_DIGEST_LEDGER_PATH); dedupes digests, so load-bearing.
Operator feedback on dot actions (dot-feedback.ts DOT_FEEDBACK_PATH); feeds later wakes' prompts.
Dot signal ledger (dot-feedback.ts DOT_SIGNAL_LEDGER_PATH); load-bearing signal history for the feedback loop.
Single-file watch-trigger snapshot (dot-runtime.ts DOT_WATCH_STATE_PATH), rewritten in place; bounded by the number of watched paths.
Single-file probe-trigger baseline/fingerprint state (dot-runtime.ts DOT_PROBE_STATE_PATH), rewritten in place.

G01: append-only reasoning backend switch log (libs/core/reasoning/reasoning-failover.ts appendReasoningFailoverEvent). Diagnostic only — no hot-path reader; the latest switch lives in runtime/state/reasoning-failover.json. Grows with failovers only; operator trims or archives.
G01: mission dispatch queue (scripts/mission_controller.ts QUEUE_PATH); pending queue state, never TTL-deleted.

Trigger-runner idempotency/claim store (libs/core/trigger-runner.ts). Self-bounding: appendRecord compacts it to the latest record per idempotency key once it would exceed maxStoreBytes (default 4 MiB), so no TTL is needed.
Dependency vulnerability ledger (libs/core/dependency-vulnerability-ledger.ts); security evidence trail.
Single-file pointer to the operator's current mission focus (mission-system.ts / agent-dispatch.ts), rewritten in place.
Active customer overlay selector written by scripts/customer_switch.ts / company_onboarding.ts; rewritten in place.
Active project scope selector (foundation/project-scope-env.ts, scope-context.ts); rewritten in place.
Delegation child-process registry (mission/delegation-concurrency.ts); the janitor's sweepDelegationChildren prunes stale rows itself.
Execution feedback store (libs/core/execution-feedback.ts); self-bounded to the newest MAX_FEEDBACK_ENTRIES (500) entries on every write.
Mutable runtime external-service registry (libs/core/external-service-registry.ts).
Intent flow cache (libs/core/intent/intent-flow-cache.ts), one file rewritten in place; entries self-expire by the policy's cache_ttl_hours, so the file carries no TTL of its own.
Applied-migration ledger (scripts/run_migrations.ts); deleting it would re-run migrations.
Pipeline scheduler registry (libs/core/pipeline/pipeline-scheduler.ts); operator-declared schedules.
Provider discovery disk cache (libs/core/provider/provider-discovery.ts), one file rewritten on every refresh — bounded by construction, regenerable.
Runtime provider capability registry (libs/core/provider/provider-capability-registry.ts).
Provider CLI capability scan report (scripts/scan_provider_cli_capabilities.ts), overwritten in place each scan — bounded by construction, regenerable.
Backend conformance report (scripts/check_backend_conformance.ts), overwritten in place each run — bounded by construction, regenerable.
Tenant rate-limiter window state (libs/core/organization/tenant-rate-limiter.ts), rewritten in place.
Live share-grant session registry (libs/core/share-grant-live-sessions.ts).
G02: one receipt per service-harness call (libs/core/service/service-harness.ts RECEIPT_DIR). Write-only execution evidence — kept ~90d like browser-receipts / voice-loopback-receipts.

G02: browser/desktop/service recordings (service-recording-session.ts, desktop-recording-compiler.ts). NOT TTL'd: procedure-catalog recording_ref entries dispatch from this store (knowledge/procedure-registry.ts resolveAllowlistedRecordingRef), so expiring a recording would break a promoted procedure.
G02: learning-signal harvest cursor/cluster state (libs/core/knowledge/learning-signal-adapter.ts STATE_DOMAIN); the adapter prunes clusters itself (CLUSTER_RETENTION_DAYS).

Tier/tenant-partitioned resource-usage ledgers (libs/core/metrics.ts RESOURCE_USAGE_LEDGER_ROOT): <tier>/<tenant|shared>/resource-usage.jsonl for usage whose scope carries a tenant or a personal/confidential tier; untenanted public usage stays in work/metrics/resource-usage.jsonl. Append-only cost/accounting evidence read by mission retrospectives, cost reports and generation-cost dedup, so no TTL deletion; personal/confidential subtrees are tenant_scope protected prefixes and follow the knowledge-tier persona read rules.

Tier/tenant-partitioned execution-metrics ledgers (libs/core/metrics.ts EXECUTION_METRICS_LEDGER_ROOT): <tier>/<tenant|shared>/execution-metrics.jsonl for MetricsCollector.record rows whose scope carries a tenant or a personal/confidential tier; untenanted public rows stay in work/metrics/execution-metrics.jsonl. Append-only latency/token/cost evidence read by cost reports, budget and spend guards, mission retrospectives and health regressions, so no TTL deletion; personal/confidential subtrees are tenant_scope protected prefixes and follow the knowledge-tier persona read rules; tenant offboarding exports and soft-deletes a tenant's partitions.
G02: discussion rooms — events, minutes.md, brief.html (libs/core/discussion/discussion-store.ts, discussion-outcomes.ts). Outcomes are referenced after the room closes; human retention decision.
G02: tenant-partitioned quarantine of rejected peer-recovery payloads (libs/core/mesh/peer-runtime-recovery.ts, scripts/backup.ts). Security evidence — never auto-deleted.
G02: Telegram bridge thread history (satellites/telegram-bridge THREAD_HISTORY_ROOT), indexed by history-search-index.ts. User conversation records — human retention decision.
G02: Discord bridge thread history (satellites/discord-bridge THREAD_HISTORY_ROOT), indexed by history-search-index.ts. User conversation records — human retention decision.
iMessage bridge event log (libs/core/imessage-bridge.ts IMESSAGE_LOG_PATH). User conversation records — human retention decision.
G02: video device lease files (libs/core/video/video-device-lease.ts); the lease manager reclaims expired/dead-pid leases itself.
Audio device lease files (libs/core/voice/audio-device-lease.ts); the lease manager reclaims expired/dead-pid leases itself.
G02: pre-migration snapshots of service bindings (service-binding-registry.ts BINDING_BACKUP_ROOT) — the rollback source for an owner migration; human decision before removal.
G02: Cloudflare OS control-plane state (libs/core/cloudflare-os-control-plane.ts control-plane.json).

G02: pipeline ADF rendered from execution plan-set bundles (orchestrator-actuator orchestrator-helpers.ts / orchestrator-execution-brief-helpers.ts). Regenerable from the bundle; consumed in the same run.
G02: delivery packs written by the artifact-actuator delivery-pack template (orchestrator-execution-brief-helpers.ts). Deliverables are never silently expired.
G02: opt-in role-assumption trace JSONL (KYBERION_ROLE_ASSUMPTION_TRACE, libs/core/organization/role-assumption-trace.ts), analyzed by scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts. Diagnostic — short TTL.
G02: tier/tenant-partitioned front-desk execution receipts (libs/core/surface/front-desk-execution.ts, front-desk-recovery-evidence.ts); recovery reads them back.
G02: managed provider-CLI installs (libs/core/provider/provider-managed-env.ts). Installed files keep old mtimes, so an mtime TTL would delete live tools; reinstall is the operator's call.
G02: staged YouTube upload packages (scripts/stage_youtube_upload_package.ts). Outbound deliverables — human decision.
G02: durable schedule declarations (scheduler-actuator scheduler-helpers.ts SCHEDULER_STORE_RELATIVE).
G02: operator seam selection rules (libs/core/seam-selection-rules.ts rules.json) — operator judgment, never auto-deleted.
Delegation notification queue (libs/core/mission/delegation-notifications.ts notifications.jsonl).
Operator-authored runtime overlay for media design themes (media-actuator media-design-protocol.ts).
Public ingress exposure state (libs/core/ingress/public-ingress-service.ts state.json).
Mandate shadow-mode decision ledger (libs/core/governance/mandate-shadow.ts); evidence for promoting shadow mandates.
PR shadow-mode decision ledger (libs/core/governance/pr-shadow.ts); evidence for promoting shadow PR policy.
Per-mission meeting briefs (scripts/meeting_orchestrator.ts).
Mission seed registry (libs/core/mission/mission-seed-registry.ts).
Per-mission provider pins (libs/core/provider/provider-pins-store.ts).
Software-quality defect event log (libs/core/software-quality-operations.ts qa/defect-events.jsonl).
Realtime voice conversation sessions (libs/core/voice/realtime-voice-conversation.ts) — conversation log, same 30d as peer-conversations / a2a-conversations.
Security-screen quarantine records (libs/core/security-screen.ts quarantineDir).
Share-grant graph state incl. its HMAC key (libs/core/share-grant-graph.ts) — deleting the key invalidates every grant.
Synthesized first-phrase audio cache (libs/core/voice/voice-first-phrase-cache.ts); self-evicting LRU (maxEntries, default 64), regenerable.
Web-push subscriptions (libs/core/surface/web-push.ts).
Outbound deliverables incl. tenant-offboarding tarballs — deletion is a human decision, never automatic.
Archived missions and long-term retention tree — deletion is a human decision, never automatic. (.trash below is the one TTL-governed exception.)

Soft-delete grace floor (AL-04): expired files from soft_delete_days entries land here preserving their original repo-relative path. The janitor trash sweep purges each file after its governing entry's soft_delete_days (30d default when no entry covers it). Code-driven — no directory-level ttl_days.

DA-08: governed tenant knowledge, including each tenant's append-only information-asset ledger (knowledge/confidential/{tenant}/_ledger/assets.jsonl, DA-05) — NEVER auto-deletable. Removal happens only through the audited tenant offboarding ceremony (scope-offboarding.ts, `pnpm kyberion offboard tenant <slug> --execute`), which exports before purging. Declared so the ledger's retention decision is explicit rather than silently uncovered. WI-10: this prefix also covers each tenant's promoted work-inventory records (knowledge/confidential/{tenant}/work-inventory/entries/*.json, calibration.json, work-inventory.ts) — same never-auto-delete, offboarding-only-removal semantics; declared here rather than as a separate entry because the tenant slug is a variable path segment this catalog's prefix matching already spans.

EV-06: cross-mission task-events.jsonl / orchestration-events.jsonl. Aligned with audit retention (90d) because agent-collaboration-projection reads these as the operator-visible history. The mission-local copy under active/missions/**/coordination/events/ is the durable record; this is the shared projection source.

AC-10: virtual (non-directory) lookup key for the dated agent-runtime-supervisor-events-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl family written by agent-runtime-events.ts's appendSupervisorEvent (rotated daily; storage-janitor.ts's sweepSupervisorEventFiles resolves this entry by exact match only, never by directory-prefix walk, so it never shadows the mission-control entry above that still governs task-events.jsonl / orchestration-events.jsonl at 90d). The pre-rotation legacy agent-runtime-supervisor-events.jsonl file is excluded from both this entry and the mission-control entry above — the janitor never auto-deletes it; an operator may archive/remove it by hand once no longer needed.
EV-06: per-surface decision/why/policy_used streams written by emitChannelSurfaceEvent. Same 30d floor as active/shared/logs — conversational surface traffic, not governance evidence.
EV-06: Chronos surface event streams (emitChronosSurfaceEvent).

EV-06: residual rule for observability files not covered by a more specific entry below — notably ops-alerts.jsonl, the sink for sendOpsAlert and for operator-notifications' undelivered-notification record of last resort. 90d so a missed alert is still discoverable at a quarterly review. scanEventStores resolves each file's owning entry by longest prefix, so channels/ and chronos/ keep their own 30d rule rather than inheriting this one.

EV-06: one JSON file per enqueued mission-orchestration event. The durable record is the orchestration journal (appendMissionOrchestrationJournalEntry), so the queue file is a work ticket, not evidence — 14d covers replay of a stalled worker without unbounded growth.

Tenant-aware surface coordination queues, notifications, outbox, dead-letter, dead-target, and physical tenant namespaces. Deletion is owned by delivery recovery or the audited tenant/project offboarding ceremony, never by TTL cleanup.
Physical namespace migration manifests and quarantined legacy records. Keep until the owner verifies the one-way cutover and explicitly decides whether quarantined records can be removed.

EV-06: the KANS stimuli journal (stimuli.jsonl) and bridge scratch state. Stimuli carry TTLs measured in seconds-to-hours and readers only consult a recent window, so 7d is already far beyond usefulness. stimuli-journal.ts additionally self-rotates at 5MB (STIMULI_MAX_BYTES) so a burst cannot outrun the daily janitor.

WI-10: self-reported work-inventory records for non-tenant-scoped personal use (work-inventory.ts's workInventoryRoot fallback) — entries/*.json and calibration.json. Same never-auto-delete, human-review-before-removal semantics as the knowledge/confidential prefix above; these are durable structured records of the member's own recurring work, not disposable scratch.

WI-10: member-scoped personal knowledge (knowledge/personal/members/<member_id>/...), including training.json (training-catalog.ts) and, for work inventory, work-inventory/consents/*.json (work-inventory-consent.ts — recording consent grants/revocations; kept while active and retained as audit evidence after revocation or expiry, the same review_required+audit norm this catalog uses for other consent/authorization evidence) and work-inventory/observations/*.json (work-inventory-observation.ts — desktop/browser recording summaries carrying a `pending_review|confirmed|discarded` status field inside each file). WI-16: the directory itself stays review_required (member_id is a variable segment, and confirmed observations plus training.json must never be swept by a blind TTL), but the two status_rules below close the per-file gap: a pending_review summary that is never confirmed, or a discarded summary, each expire 30 days after their own status transition — confirmed summaries and consent records are never matched by either rule and are never auto-deleted. Status rules are the one explicit, opt-in exception to 'review_required never deletes': a rule's own action 'delete' deletes only files matching its path_pattern whose status is one of its statuses and past its ttl.
